definition.explanation: A decimal number is a number that contains a decimal point, separating the whole number part from the fractional part. Decimals are another way to represent parts of a whole, just like fractions.

placeValue.title: Decimal Place Value
placeValue.description: Each digit in a decimal number has a place value based on its position relative to the decimal point.
placeValue.numberReading: The number 246.357 is read as "two hundred forty-six point three five seven" or "two hundred forty-six and three hundred fifty-seven thousandths"

pronunciation.title: 💡 Pronunciation Tip:
pronunciation.point: The decimal point (•) is read as "point" or "and"

placeValueMemory.title: 🎯 Easy Trick - Place Value Memory:
placeValueMemory.pattern: Each place is 10 times smaller than the one before!

comparing.title: 🎯 Comparing Trick - "Add Zeros Method":
comparing.method1Title: Method 1: Add zeros to make same length
comparing.method2Title: Method 2: Remove decimal, compare as whole numbers
comparing.method3Example: Which is closer to 1? That's the bigger one!

addSubtract.title: 💡 Adding/Subtracting Trick - "Line Up Method":
addSubtract.step2: Step 2: Line up decimal points (one under the other)
addSubtract.step3: Step 3: Add zeros to make same length (optional but helpful!)
addSubtract.memory: Memory trick: "Decimals are shy - they never move during +/−"

multiply.title: ⚡ Multiplying Trick - "Count & Place":
multiply.quickCheck:
Quick Check: If multiplying by 0.1, move decimal LEFT 1 place
Example: 5 × 0.1 = 0.5 (5.0 → 0.5)

divide.title: 💡 Division Tricks - Multiple Methods:
divide.quickTip:
Quick tip: Dividing by 0.1 = Multiply by 10
Example: 5 ÷ 0.1 = 50 (move decimal right!)

commonMistakes.title: Common Mistakes:
commonMistakes.mistake1: Not lining up decimal points when adding/subtracting
commonMistakes.mistake2: Forgetting to count decimal places when multiplying

placeValue.question: What is the place value of the digit 7 in 42.378?
placeValue.explanation: In 42.378, the 7 is in the hundredths place (second digit after the decimal point). The 3 is in tenths, 7 is in hundredths, and 8 is in thousandths.
placeValue.hint: Count positions from the decimal point: first position = tenths, second position = hundredths

multiplication.question: What is 0.4 × 0.5?
multiplication.explanation: 4 × 5 = 20. With 2 decimal places total, answer is 0.20 = 0.2

wordProblem.question: A book costs $12.50 and a pen costs $2.75. What is the total?

fractionToDecimal.title: Converting Fractions to Decimals
fractionToDecimal.explanation: To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator.

decimalToFraction.explanation: To convert a decimal to a fraction:

conclusion.title: Excellent work!
conclusion.message: You've learned about decimal numbers, place value, converting between fractions and decimals, and all four operations with decimals. Decimals are essential for money, measurements, and many real-world applications!
